C22.label: defeated

C22.text: With age, the absolute bleeding burden and the modelled net balance worsen (net loss of QALYs/life-years at 70-79), while relative effects of aspirin do not differ by age

C23.label: contested
C23.reason: standing pro and con arguments prevent an accepted answer
C23.text: Relative effects of aspirin on cardiovascular events and bleeding are reported as not differing significantly by age or baseline risk in most trials, while absolute benefit and bleeding harm are greater at higher risk and older age.

C24.label: defeated
C24.reason: all constructed support is out, withdrawn or inapplicable
C24.text: In adults 70+ without prior CVD (ASPREE), starting low-dose aspirin increased major haemorrhage (HR 1.38, 95% CI 1.18-1.62; about 1 percentage point absolute excess over a median 4.7 years) and all-cause mortality (HR 1.14, 95% CI 1.01-1.29); no MACE estimate is available in the sources, so the net cardiovascular balance was not measured directly

C25.label: insufficient
C25.reason: standing unopposed support is below the proof standard
C25.text: Aspirin increased aggregate major haemorrhage in adults 70+ (ASPREE HR 1.38, 1.18-1.62; 3.8% vs 2.8%), and pooled all-age trials show major GI bleeding OR 1.58 (1.38-1.80) and intracranial bleeding OR 1.31 (1.11-1.54); the USPSTF judges bleeding harm larger at older ages

C26.label: defeated
C26.reason: all constructed support is out, withdrawn or inapplicable
C26.text: In pooled primary-prevention trials of mixed ages, low-dose aspirin modestly reduced nonfatal MI (Peto OR 0.88, 0.80-0.96) and borderline nonfatal ischaemic stroke (OR 0.88, 0.78-1.00), with no significant effect on fatal outcomes; these are all-age results and not specific to adults 60+

C27.text: USPSTF concluded with moderate certainty that initiating aspirin for primary prevention in adults 60+ has no net benefit (a verdict of 'no net benefit', not 'net harm')

C28.text: In ASPREE (70+) and ARRIVE (55+), reports describe no significant difference in cardiovascular composite outcomes with aspirin; no effect estimates or CIs are available in the retrieved sources, so a small benefit is not excluded
